Chapter 3. Quick Start

Source: vignettes/articles/03-Quick-Start.Rmd
03-Quick-Start.Rmd

This chapter runs a complete analysis on simulated data in which the true contamination is known, so you can see Decant recover it.

3.1 Simulate an experiment 

library(Decant)
sim <- simulate_experiment(seed = 1)
dim(sim$observed)
#> [1]  600 1200
dim(sim$empty)
#> [1]  600 4000
  • simulate_experiment(seed = 1) creates a contaminated experiment with 600 genes, 1,200 cells of six cell types, and 4,000 empty droplets. The seed makes the result identical every time.
  • sim$observed holds the contaminated cell counts (genes × cells).
  • sim$empty holds the empty droplets (genes × droplets).
  • The simulation also stores the answer: sim$truth (the clean counts), sim$rho_true (each cell’s true contamination) and sim$labels (the cell types).

3.2 Run Decant 

res <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty, clusters = sim$labels)
res
#> <decant> 600 genes x 1200 cells
#>   modules : cluster_rho, correction_bayes_cell
#>   rho     : median 0.199 (10%-90%: 0.117-0.305)
  • decant() takes the cell counts, the empty droplets and the cluster labels, and returns a result object.
  • Printing the result shows its size, the steps that ran (modules) and a summary of the estimated contamination: the median cell is 19.9% ambient, and 80% of cells lie between 11.7% and 30.5%.

3.3 Compare with the truth 

summary(res$rho)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> 0.02389 0.14950 0.19933 0.20574 0.25223 0.55303 
summary(sim$rho_true)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.0148  0.1371  0.1907  0.1970  0.2473  0.5317 
cor(res$rho, sim$rho_true)
#> [1] 0.9760583
  • res$rho is the estimated contamination of every cell.
  • The estimates sit slightly above the truth here (median 0.199 against 0.191), and the correlation of 0.98 shows Decant ranks cells correctly.

3.4 Score the correction 

score_correction(sim$observed, sim$observed, sim$truth)$l1_error
#> [1] 0.2451949
score_correction(sim$observed, res$corrected, sim$truth)$l1_error
#> [1] 0.04877535
  • score_correction() compares a matrix with the clean truth. Its l1_error adds up every count that is wrong, whether contamination left behind or real signal removed, as a fraction of the true total.
  • Without correction (first line) 24.5% of counts are wrong. After Decant the error falls to 4.9%.

3.5 Use the corrected counts 

corrected <- res$corrected
all(corrected <= sim$observed)
#> [1] TRUE
  • res$corrected has the same genes, cells and class as the input and can be used wherever you would use raw counts.
  • The check confirms that no count was increased.

3.6 With your own data 

# Requires your own data
library(Decant)
raw   <- read_10x_counts("sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
cells <- colnames(read_10x_counts("sample/outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))
d     <- split_droplets(raw, cells = cells)
res   <- decant(d$cells, d$empties, clusters = my_clusters)
  • read_10x_counts() reads a Cell Ranger folder into a sparse matrix.
  • The filtered matrix is read only for its column names, the barcodes Cell Ranger called as cells.
  • split_droplets() separates the raw matrix into cells and empty droplets.
  • my_clusters is a vector with one cluster label per cell, in the same order as the columns of d$cells, for example from Seurat.

Chapter 4 explains each of these steps.
